title: Framing of charges - an underrated turning point in a trial
p1:
Many people think a trial truly begins when witnesses enter the courtroom.

But a major turning point often happens much earlier — when the court decides what exactly the accused will face.
p2: This stage is called framing of charges, and it is often misunderstood. It does not mean the person is guilty. It simply means the court has found enough material to formally state the allegations that need to be tested during the trial.
p3:
The interesting part? A wrongly framed charge can change the entire direction of a case. The issues, evidence, and questions asked in court all revolve around these charges. A clear framing ensures the trial focuses only on the real disputes instead of becoming a confusing search for facts.

For anyone following a criminal case, this stage is a reminder that every trial has a roadmap — and framing of charges creates that roadmap.
conclusion: Did you know that a trial’s direction can often be shaped before the first witness is even examined? What are your thoughts on the role of framing of charges?
